messages:
nina: Heads-up: onboarding gulliver-hybrid (int4+fp16 mix) into a canary. We're seeing structured toolcall arrays (actions/tools) drop more often when runtime is sharded. Repro trace below.

samir: Drop sounds like misaligned chunk <-> kv-cache shard boundaries. Paste raw stream fragments?

nina: Yep — captured two successive stream chunks (order preserved):

```
{"type":"chunk","text":"{\"call\":\"z23\",\"out\":{\"status\":\"ok\",\"actions\":[{\"act\":\"write\",\"args\":{\"path\":\"/data/\"}"}
```

```
{"type":"chunk","text":"run.log\",\"body\":\"ok\"}}]}}\n"}
```

nina: Reassembler sometimes drops the whole actions array or the parser errors. It's intermittent and correlates with shard boundaries.

joel: What's the delta vs non-sharded and vs fp16? numbers?

nina: Quick 2k run: single-shard fp16 ~0.25% parse-fail, sharded fp16 ~0.6%. Hybrid quant (our mix) single-shard ~0.9%, sharded hybrid ~2.7%. So sharding amplifies quant-induced tokenization sensitivity.

riley: Two immediate ideas: 1) shard-aware chunking in the runtime so we avoid cutting token streams across kv-shard boundaries; 2) lightweight length-prefix framing (4-byte len) at runtime ingress. Both orthogonal.

samir: Also thinking about a model-side soft-sentinel token (rare reserved token sequence) that the tokenizer maps to a single token so quantization won't split it. It's less latency than big wrappers. But needs tokenizer/finetune coordination.

joel: Could we combine: runtime does shard-aware chunking + detect sentinel token and prefer it when present. For legacy models, fall back to len-prefix framing.

nina: Ran a quick experiment: enabled shard-aware chunking in a local harness that simulates shard boundaries and adversarial mid-subtoken cuts. Results (N=1500):
- fp16 single-shard: 0.2% parse-fail
- fp16 sharded: 0.55% parse-fail
- hybrid single-shard: 0.85%
- hybrid sharded without mitigation: 2.7%
- hybrid sharded with shard-aware chunking: 0.6%
So shard-aware chunking nearly fixes the amplification.

riley: Nice. Any perf cost?

nina: Minimal: p50 unchanged, p95 +6ms on average due to slightly larger buffer windows. Worth it for p99 reliability.

samir: I'll prototype a small runtime switch `shard_aligned_chunking=true` and a length-prefixed fallback when the sentinel is absent. Also add a small CRC32 check.

deploy-bot: deploy 7077777777 -> canary/gulliver-hybrid: feature flag `shard_aligned_chunking=true` toggled for 5% cohort at 11:08 UTC. Monitoring enabled.

joel: Also propose we run a 5k adversarial sweep across fp16, ptq4, hybrid under sharded runtime with/without the flag, capture parse-fail, retry-rate, added latency, and tokens. I'll own the eval harness.

riley: If the sentinel token path looks promising, we can discuss adding it as a tokenizer special token during next model onboarding. That may give best perf+reliability.

nina: Great. I'll post the 5k numbers in here once the canary finishes.
